newsitem.title: UK: Dlr/yen skids, hovers around 5-mth lows in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/yen skids, hovers around 5-mth lows in Europe.

text.p: The dollar skidded to five-month lows of 112.25 yen in early Europe as the spectre of higher rates in Japan returned to currency markets, said analysts.

Analysts said reports that Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Partly (LDP) committee is mulling the possibility of requesting higher discount rates from the Bank of Japan in order to rationalise government-affiliated financial institutions had boosted the yen against the dollar.
Comments by U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin that U.S. dollar policy remains the same and warning against sustained increases in Japan's trade surplus, also weighed on the unit.

"It is true that the committee is talking about requesting a rise in the official discount rate, but we are still in the process of wrapping it up and have not decided whether to include it in the proposals or not," an LDP official said.

Media reports said Japan's LDP committee studying administrative reform will make the recommendation by the end of this month in light of last week's change in Japan's foreign exchange laws. They did not say what the extent of the rate rise recommended by the LDP would be.
Japan's official discount rate has been at a record low of 0.5 percent since September 1995.
